summary: This bill amends federal education law to prohibit schools and programs receiving federal funds from allowing males, defined by birth reproductive biology and genetics, to participate in sports teams or activities designated for females.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends Title IX to regulate athletic participation based on biological sex and requires a single study by the Comptroller General. This mandates minimal government activity and potential minor spending for the study, but it does not expand or reduce overall government spending in any meaningful way. No appropriations, cuts, or budgetary impacts are specified. Thus, no bearing on government spending.
The bill text contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or fiscal policy. It solely addresses Title IX compliance in educational athletics.
No references to healthcare, insurance, medical coverage, or health policy. The bill focuses on sports participation in educational settings.
The bill has no content related to firearms, regulations, or rights.
No mention of immigration, borders, or related policies.
The bill does not address abortion access, restrictions, or reproductive rights beyond defining sex by biology for sports purposes.
No provisions on military, defense, or related spending.
No environmental regulations, climate policies, or protections mentioned.
No welfare, food stamps, or safety net programs involved.

The bill directly amends Section 901 of the Education Amendments of 1972 (Title IX), imposing federal requirements on schools and institutions receiving federal aid regarding sex-based athletic participation. This increases federal regulatory involvement in public school and educational athletics policies, aligning with greater federal oversight rather than privatization or school choice. It mandates compliance for federal funding recipients, moderately enhancing federal involvement in education.
No drug-related enforcement, decriminalization, or policies.

The required study mentions psychological and sociological impacts including sexual assault/harassment environments but does not enact criminal justice reforms, sentencing, or policing changes. Tangential at best, no direct relation.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization content.
No deficit spending, debt reduction, or fiscal prioritization. Minor study has negligible impact.

The bill prohibits males (defined by birth biology/genetics) from participating in female-designated athletic programs/activities under Title IX, effectively barring transgender women/girls from women's sports in federally funded education settings. This limits legal access and protections for transgender individuals (LGBTQ+) in athletics, strongly pushing toward limiting such protections rather than expanding them. Primary focus of the bill.
No foreign aid provisions.
No voting access, elections, or integrity measures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight.
No labor protections, unions, or employer policies.
The bill addresses sex discrimination in sports based on biology, not religious liberty, exemptions, or anti-discrimination prioritizing civil rights vs. religion. No religious content.
